# Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-14 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Running Ollama on Windows as a real system service is not provided by the installer: the docs point to the standalone ollama-windows-amd64.zip (CLI plus NVIDIA libs; add ollama-windows-amd64-rocm.zip for AMD) run via `ollama serve` under a wrapper such as NSSM. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows

## How it works

- [statement] On Linux, the documented install is `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`; the manual path extracts ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst (plus ollama-linux-amd64-rocm.tar.zst for AMD, or the arm64 package) into /usr. When upgrading manually, remove /usr/lib/ollama first. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/linux
- [statement] On Linux the service runs as user `ollama`, so a custom OLLAMA_MODELS directory must be readable and writable by that user (and its parent path traversable). A root-owned /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models after a sudo install causes 'permission denied' for other apps sharing that path, such as Msty. (medium confidence) — https://docs.msty.app/troubleshooting/linux-issues · keywords: Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows · also: https://docs.ollama.com/linux

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To set server environment variables under systemd, run `sudo systemctl edit ollama.service` (creates /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf), add `[Service]` plus `Environment="NAME=value"` lines, then `systemctl daemon-reload` and `systemctl restart ollama`. Do not edit the packaged unit file; package updates overwrite it. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows · also: https://docs.ollama.com/linux, https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening
- [statement] To pin a version on Linux, run the install script with `OLLAMA_VERSION=<version>` (pre-releases allowed). Updating is re-running the install script or re-extracting the tarball. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/linux

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Behind an nginx reverse proxy, rewrite the Host header to localhost:11434 (or list the external hostname in OLLAMA_ORIGINS) to avoid 403 Forbidden; turn off proxy_buffering and raise proxy_read_timeout so streamed generations are not cut at ~60 s. (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows · also: https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The documented manual systemd setup creates a system user and group `ollama` (home /usr/share/ollama, shell /bin/false), adds the current user to that group, and writes /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service with ExecStart=/usr/bin/ollama serve, User=ollama, Restart=always, RestartSec=3, WantedBy=multi-user.target; then daemon-reload and enable/start. Logs are read with `journalctl -e -u ollama`. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/linux
- [statement] A drop-in saved without the `[Service]` header is silently ignored, and a variable exported in a user shell never reaches the systemd-run daemon (the CLI is only an HTTP client). Verify with `systemctl show ollama.service -p Environment` and `ss -tlnp | grep 11434`. (medium confidence) — https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening · keywords: Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] Ollama binds 127.0.0.1:11434 by default; OLLAMA_HOST changes the bind address (e.g. 0.0.0.0:11434 for all interfaces, or a single private IP). The API has no built-in authentication or rate limiting, so exposing it needs a firewall source-subnet rule or a reverse proxy with auth and TLS. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows · also: https://www.centron.de/tutorials/expose-ollama-network-port-hardening
- [statement] On Windows, OllamaSetup.exe installs per-user without Administrator rights (default under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Ollama, PATH updated for the user); `OllamaSetup.exe /DIR="d:\some\location"` relocates the binaries. Requirements: Windows 10 22H2 or newer and NVIDIA driver 551.61+ for NVIDIA cards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows
- [statement] On Windows, Ollama inherits user and system environment variables. Set OLLAMA_HOST, OLLAMA_MODELS etc. under 'Edit environment variables for your account', then quit the tray application and relaunch it from the Start menu (or open a new terminal). If OLLAMA_MODELS was changed, the uninstaller does not remove downloaded models. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows · keywords: Ollama installation and service ops on Linux and Windows · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] On Windows, logs live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama (app.log for the GUI, server.log for the server, upgrade.log); models and config default to %HOMEPATH%\.ollama. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/windows
